claim: The Linux kernel hardcodes mode 0400 on /sys/class/dmi/id/{product_serial,product_uuid,board_serial,chassis_serial} and 0444 on every other DMI attribute.
design_impact: Vendor/model/family ARE readable at uid 1000; serial and UUID are NOT. Machine identity must use a fallback ladder ending in explicit unknown, and 'serial unknown' is correct behaviour, not a sensor defect.

claim: Every raw SMBIOS acquisition route is root-only: /sys/firmware/dmi/tables/{DMI,smbios_entry_point} are S_IRUSR (dmi_scan.c:757-758), /sys/firmware/efi/systab is 0400 (efi/efi.c:157), and /dev/mem is root:kmem.
design_impact: No SMBIOS-parsing library can beat direct sysfs reads unprivileged; the data is simply out of reach for all of them. Kills u-root/pkg/smbios, digitalocean/go-smbios and dmidecode as options in one stroke.

claim: ghw converts any DMI read error, including EACCES, into the untyped literal string "unknown" with no errno and no error return (pkg/linuxdmi/dmi_linux.go:33-37 via pkg/util/util.go:20).
design_impact: Fatal for our contract: a finding needs a reason and an errno. ghw destroys exactly the information the schema requires. REJECT as evidence layer.

claim: ghw's README states "No root privileges needed for discovery" (README:14) while the same README later documents permission-denied warnings (README:1045-1051).
design_impact: The prompt's target contradiction, confirmed at source. Documented capability claims about unprivileged behaviour must be checked against code, never trusted.

claim: ghw's Linux memory path scrapes /var/log/syslog for installed RAM and silently substitutes usable-for-installed when that fails (pkg/memory/memory_linux.go:28,41-52,209-236).
design_impact: On the Lava host the login user is in 'ubuntu sudo' but NOT 'adm', so syslog is unreadable and ghw would silently report usable RAM as installed RAM. A wrong number with no unknown marker is the worst possible outcome under contract B6.

claim: gopsutil's HostID() returns ("", nil) on total failure rather than an error.
design_impact: Empty string is explicitly forbidden by the brief ('an empty string or a plausible guess is worse than a field that admits it does not know'). STEAL its host-id ladder, do not REUSE the function.

claim: prometheus/procfs sysfs/class_dmi.go models every DMI field as *string, reads regular files only (:64), and has an explicit os.IsPermission(err) -> continue branch commented "Only root is allowed to read the serial and product_uuid files!" (:74-81).
design_impact: The only library that already models unprivileged DMI correctly. Pointer-or-nil is the Go shape for 'explicit unknown'. REUSE candidate, and at minimum the pattern to copy.

claim: zcalusic/sysinfo requires superuser for SMBIOS/DMI and RAM properties; its shipped example log.Fatal()s when run as non-root.
design_impact: REJECT outright. A library that aborts the process when unprivileged is disqualified by safety requirement E3 alone.

claim: osquery is dual-licensed 'Apache-2.0 OR GPL-2.0-only' and the consumer chooses; the SPDX header appears in each source file.
design_impact: Re-implementing osquery techniques under the Apache-2.0 arm is licence-clean. Lynis (GPLv3), Wazuh (GPLv2) and FreeIPMI (GPLv3) are behaviour references only, never code sources.

claim: osquery's disk_encryption table returns ZERO ROWS when non-root (disk_encryption.cpp:111-114), which is indistinguishable from 'nothing is encrypted'.
design_impact: Canonical false-negative. On the Lava host (no dm-crypt at all) our answer must be 'proven absent by successful listing', which requires evidence osquery does not produce.

claim: blkid run as uid 1000 prints nothing and exits without error, because /dev/sd* and /dev/nvme* are brw-rw---- root:disk.
design_impact: Silent empty success is worse than an error. Never shell out to blkid; read filesystem identity from the world-readable udev database instead.

claim: Disk model, serial, WWN, fstype and UUID are available unprivileged from the world-readable udev database at /run/udev/data/b<major>:<minor> (as gopsutil does at disk_linux.go:604-664).
design_impact: Recovers most of what lsblk/blkid would give, with no subprocess and no device open. Primary storage-inventory route; sysfs is the fallback when udev data is absent.

claim: Installed RAM (memory blocks x block size) and kernel-visible MemTotal differ materially: LOCAL_REPRO measured 63 blocks x 128 MiB = 8064 MiB installed vs MemTotal 7721 MiB.
design_impact: 'Memory' is ambiguous. Report MemTotal with memory_source naming the file, and treat installed capacity as a separate, clearly-labelled field. Do not let one stand in for the other.

claim: The R1 brief's premise that gitleaks was relicensed away from MIT is FALSE: gitleaks is MIT at HEAD (v8.30.1) and its LICENSE file has three commits total, newest 2019-12-04.
design_impact: Corrects our own brief. gitleaks must be rejected for real reasons (R1-F15), not a licence myth. Repeating the myth in NOTES.md would be a checkable error in front of the customer.

claim: gitleaks does not redact by default (--redact defaults to 0 at cmd/root.go:86-87; NoOptDefVal=100 applies only to a bare flag) and its report serialises the raw Secret and Match fields, with only Line excluded (report/finding.go:14-55).
design_impact: Decisive. Embedding gitleaks would turn our own findings.json into a NEW secret-bearing artifact on the customer's disk. This is a safety verdict, not a preference.

claim: trufflehog is AGPL-3.0 and verifies discovered credentials against live third-party APIs BY DEFAULT (--no-verification is opt-out; main.go:60, main.go:643 Verify: !*noVerification); 430 modules vs gitleaks' 144.
design_impact: Two independent hard blockers: copyleft licence, and outbound network calls carrying the customer's credentials. Violates E1a in the worst possible way.

claim: POSIX ACLs are readable and decodable in pure Go from the system.posix_acl_access xattr: version 0x0002 followed by 8-byte {le16 tag, le16 perm, le32 id} entries (kernel UAPI posix_acl_xattr.h:24,29-37). Byte-verified locally on a machine with no getfacl/setfacl/getfattr installed: /var/log/journal returned 44 bytes = 4 + 8*5, decoding to the exact systemd ACL group:4(adm):r-x.
design_impact: Retires the 'getfacl is absent on the host so ACLs are UNKNOWN' blocker. ~30 lines of unix.Getxattr plus binary.LittleEndian gives a real 'who can read this' answer, which is exactly what the SECRETS_ON_DISK and BMC categories are asked for.

claim: OpenSSH's private key format puts ciphername second in the header and the encrypted key material structurally last (PROTOCOL.key:8-19), so ciphername=="none" proves an unencrypted on-disk SSH key from roughly the first 48 decoded bytes.
design_impact: A genuinely valuable secrets finding (unencrypted private key) obtained with provably zero leak risk. This is the single best argument that header-only classification beats content scanning.

claim: gitleaks' private-key regex (gitleaks.toml:2784-2788) must consume at least 64 characters of the base64 key body to match.
design_impact: Content scanning inherently ingests key material; header-only classification does not. Justifies rejecting the entire content-scanning capability as a scope decision to declare in NOTES.md.

claim: lstat-first is mandatory and O_NONBLOCK is not sufficient: LOCAL_REPRO showed cat on a FIFO hanging for the full timeout (exit=124) while lstat reported S_ISFIFO before any open.
design_impact: Directly satisfies E2 ('nothing hangs forever on a device that does not answer'). The rule is: lstat, confirm S_ISREG, only then open.

claim: openat2 with RESOLVE_NO_SYMLINKS requires Linux 5.6+.
design_impact: Optional hardening behind an ENOSYS capability-detection fallback, never the mechanism and never a kernel-version string comparison. Genericity requirement F1.

claim: EACCES on a FILE after a successful lstat is a complete answer (the file exists and we may not read it); EACCES on readdir is a genuine UNKNOWN (we cannot enumerate, so absence is unprovable).
design_impact: Named as the likeliest bug in the secrets check family. Encodes the project law 'absence is only provable from a successful listing' as a concrete code rule.

claim: /dev/ipmiN is 0600 root:root because ipmi_devintf registers a class with no .devnode callback (ipmi_devintf.c:810-812, :827) and devtmpfs defaults to 0600 when no devnode mode is supplied (devtmpfs.c:12, :122-130; core.c:3913-3931).
design_impact: Closed proof. EACCES on /dev/ipmi0 is the stock upstream Linux default, NOT a Supermicro or Latitude.sh hardening choice. The sensor must report it as normal, not as a misconfiguration.

claim: The IPMI chrdev registers the name "ipmidev" (ipmi_devintf.c:792, :869) while the node is named ipmi%d (:827), so world-readable /proc/devices shows '<major> ipmidev' and never 'ipmi0'.
design_impact: A second, always-permitted evidence path proving the driver holds a major even under EACCES. A sensor grepping /proc/devices for 'ipmi0' finds nothing and wrongly concludes absence.

claim: The BMC sysfs attributes under /sys/devices/platform/ipmi_bmc.N/ are 0444 and yield IPMI version, firmware revision, manufacturer id, product id, device id and GUID unprivileged.
design_impact: This is the whole BMC_INBAND_ACCESS answer without ever touching the device node: the same payload a Get Device ID would return, with no privilege and no hang risk. No existing tool we found uses it.

claim: /sys/firmware/dmi/entries/ subdirectories are 0755 and listable while their contents are 0400, and the directory names encode '<type>-<instance>' (dmi-sysfs.c:607-608; sysfs dir mode 0755 at fs/sysfs/dir.c:59).
design_impact: Converts a root-only data source into an unprivileged presence oracle: readdir proves firmware declares SMBIOS type 38 (IPMI device) and type 42 (Redfish host interface) without reading a byte of root-only data.

claim: ipmitool's open-interface probe (src/plugins/open/open.c:102-118) tries /dev/ipmi0, /dev/ipmi/0 and /dev/ipmidev/0 but overwrites errno on each retry and reports only the last, so an EACCES on the first path is reported as ENOENT.
design_impact: Mature prior art misreports 'not permitted' as 'not present' — precisely the failure the brief calls a critical failure. Steal the path list, invert the control flow, retain errno per path.

claim: u-root's pkg/ipmi opens the device with os.OpenFile(path, os.O_RDWR, 0), so it can do nothing at all against a 0600 root:root node.
design_impact: Licence (BSD-3) and language (Go, CGO-free) are fine and still irrelevant: the capability is zero-valued unprivileged. Capability-fidelity in one line.

claim: osquery has NO IPMI/BMC table in master; a 2017 attempt was closed unmerged over native-library and per-vendor BMC breakage.
design_impact: Proven absence by search, not assumed. There is no prior art to reuse for BMC in-band posture, which strengthens the BUILD verdict and makes this category a genuine differentiator.

claim: Files in /sys/firmware/efi/efivars/ carry 4 bytes of UEFI attributes in little-endian BEFORE the variable data.
design_impact: Read 5 bytes and take index 4. A reader that takes byte 0 reports Secure Boot state confidently and wrongly.

claim: /sys/firmware/efi/efivars is world readable while the older /sys/firmware/efi/vars is root-only, and osquery chose efivars specifically because 'the benefit of not requiring root outweighs' the nicer format (secureboot.cpp @5.15.0).
design_impact: Secure Boot posture IS establishable at uid 1000; mokutil is an optional cross-check, never the mechanism. Generalises into a design law: when two paths give the same fact, take the one that works unprivileged and record the rejected path.

claim: osquery's Secure Boot table silently emits no row when the efivar read fails: 'if (!readFile(efivarPath, efiData, 5).ok()) { return; }'.
design_impact: Mature prior art commits exactly the silent-omission failure the brief calls critical. Our runner must emit one finding per registered check by construction. Strong NOTES.md contrast material.

claim: /proc/sys/kernel/tainted bit 12 (4096) = 'O' out-of-tree module, bit 13 (8192) = 'E' unsigned module; 12288 = both. The file is world-readable.
design_impact: The host's 12288 decodes to a defensible 'unsigned, out-of-tree module loaded' finding. Embed the kernel's own bit table as data so evidence reads as a decode, not a bare integer.

claim: /sys/devices/system/cpu/vulnerabilities/* are mode 0444, one file per vulnerability, and the file SET is kernel-version dependent (recent kernels add ghostwrite, indirect_target_selection).
design_impact: A fully unprivileged check with no fallback logic — but enumerate the directory rather than hardcoding a list, or the check silently under-reports on other kernels.

claim: With kptr_restrict=1, /proc/kallsyms returns a SUCCESSFUL read of zeroed addresses to a non-root reader rather than failing.
design_impact: A third failure mode beyond EACCES and ENOENT: read-succeeded-but-content-degraded. No prior art we read flags it. Any check consuming kernel addresses must treat all-zero as 'restricted', never as a value.

claim: On a kernel without the lockdown LSM, /sys/kernel/security/ is dr-xr-xr-x and traversable by uid 1000 but empty, so reading lockdown returns ENOENT, not EACCES.
design_impact: ENOENT (feature absent, often a legitimate info) and EACCES (present, not permitted, a true unknown) are different reasons and must not be collapsed. Also withdraws our own briefing assumption that securityfs is root-only.

claim: /sys/firmware/efi is absent entirely on a non-UEFI system, making its existence the correct UEFI-vs-legacy discriminator; /sys/class/dmi/id is likewise absent on WSL2.
design_impact: Genericity: on a BIOS host 'Secure Boot disabled' would be a FALSE fail. Correct output is an explicit not-applicable with reason. The local WSL lab exercises the no-DMI and no-EFI branches for free.

claim: github.com/santhosh-tekuri/jsonschema/v6 v6.0.3 is Apache-2.0 and supports draft-04, draft-06, draft-07, 2019-09 and 2020-12 (draft.go L27/L53/L66/L80/L103).
design_impact: The only candidate correct under all three possible answers to the unknown schema draft. Removes draft risk from the decision entirely.

claim: santhosh-tekuri/jsonschema v6 defaults to 2020-12 when the schema omits $schema (draftLatest = Draft2020, draft.go:124).
design_impact: A draft-07 schema with no $schema would be validated under 2020-12 semantics ($ref siblings, non-tuple items) and could pass locally but fail on Lava's validator. Drives observation request R1-OR1.

claim: Measured: santhosh-tekuri/jsonschema/v6 v6.0.3 pulls exactly 2 modules (itself + golang.org/x/text v0.14.0) and links 15 non-stdlib packages; dlclark/regexp2 is optional and not in the build graph.
design_impact: Measured with the real toolchain, not claimed from a README. Smallest full-draft validator footprint available.

claim: xeipuuv/gojsonschema v1.2.0 supports only draft-04/06/07 (its own README) and its two dependencies are pinned to 2018 pseudo-versions.
design_impact: REJECT. Popularity is not draft coverage; if the real schema is 2019-09 or 2020-12 this library cannot validate it at all.

claim: kaptinlin/jsonschema v0.9.9 silently raised the toolchain requirement during go get ('go: upgraded go 1.26.2 => 1.27') and drags goccy/go-yaml, go-i18n, messageformat-go, cockroachdb/apd/v3, google/uuid and go-json-experiment/json.
design_impact: REJECT. A tarball that must build reproducibly cannot afford a silent toolchain bump, and a YAML+i18n stack has no place in a posture sensor.

claim: A package imported only from _test.go files is not in go list -deps for the main package and is not linked into the binary.
design_impact: Decisive reframing: schema validation is a TEST capability, not a runtime one. The shipped binary keeps zero third-party runtime dependencies for conformance and the supply-chain question leaves the customer-facing artifact.

claim: golang.org/x/sys (v0.48.0) is BSD-3-Clause, pure Go with no cgo, and resolved as a single module with no transitive requirements; it supplies Getxattr, Statfs, Openat2, Faccessat, Ioctl, Uname.
design_impact: The one runtime dependency worth taking. Required for the pure-Go ACL reader (R1-F17), filesystem-boundary detection and openat2 hardening.

claim: exec.CommandContext by default kills only the direct child ('sets the command's Cancel function to invoke the Kill method on its Process, and leaves its WaitDelay unset') and Wait blocks until stdout/stderr copying completes.
design_impact: The naive exec.CommandContext(ctx,...).Output() that an LLM emits by default does NOT satisfy E2: a grandchild holding the pipes makes Wait block past the deadline.

claim: Cmd.WaitDelay bounds exactly the two unexpected delays in Wait — a child that fails to exit after cancellation, and a child that exits leaving its I/O pipes unclosed — closing the pipes on expiry to unblock readers.
design_impact: Highest-value single line in the bounded-execution design. Combine WaitDelay with SysProcAttr{Setpgid:true} and a Cancel that kills the process group.

claim: Reading the 'safe' 0444 BMC sysfs attributes triggers a LIVE IPMI transaction (device_id_show -> send_get_device_id_cmd), and KCS timeouts are 5s IBF + 5s OBF with up to 10 retries (ipmi_kcs_sm.c:103-106), matching IPMI v2.0 section 9.20.
design_impact: CRITICAL and counter-intuitive: the unprivileged sysfs read is NOT free. Against a wedged BMC it can block for tens of seconds inside read(), and a Go goroutine cannot be cancelled mid-syscall. The BMC check needs an out-of-band deadline (separate goroutine plus whole-scan budget, result abandoned on timeout) rather than a naive context, and must degrade to a cached/UNKNOWN finding. This is exactly the 'nothing hangs forever on a device that does not answer' case the brief names.

claim: The BMC 'guid' attribute is only exposed when the kernel actually obtained one from the controller (ipmi_msghandler.c:2941-2946).
design_impact: Its presence is transitive proof that the kernel completed a real KCS transaction with the BMC. In-band reachability becomes provable without ever opening /dev/ipmi0 — a genuinely novel unprivileged evidence path.

claim: All ten BMC identity attributes under /sys/devices/platform/ipmi_bmc.N/ are mode 0444 (ipmi_msghandler.c:2758-2911, mode via sysfs.h:115-118).
design_impact: Confirms R1-F25 at kernel-source level rather than by host observation alone.

claim: OpenSSH 9.6p1 has `sshd -G`, which dumps the effective configuration BEFORE host-key loading (sshd.c:1619-1620 and :1815-1816, versus the key loop at :1831-1936 and the fatal at :1933-1936), so it works as uid 1000 where `sshd -T` cannot.
design_impact: OVERTURNS the assumption that effective sshd policy is root-only. `sshd -T` fails with 'no hostkeys available -- exiting' precisely because it loads keys first; `-G` returns before that point. This becomes our unprivileged effective-config oracle, subject to R1-OR9 confirming it on the host.

claim: `sshd -G -C <connspec>` FATALS at sshd.c:1741-1747 even though sshd.8:157-165 documents the combination as supported.
design_impact: Man page and code disagree; the code wins. Our ceiling is the GLOBAL effective config with no Match-block evaluation. Match-conditional policy must be reported as a separate, explicitly-bounded unknown rather than silently folded into the global answer.

claim: OpenSSH is first-match-wins (servconf.c:108/139 sentinels with guards at :1404/:1485/:1555), and `Include` expands INLINE, glob-sorted, and is non-fatal when it matches nothing (servconf.c:2128-2215). Ubuntu puts `Include /etc/ssh/sshd_config.d/*.conf` on line 1, so the drop-in WINS.
design_impact: A sensor that reads sshd_config top-to-bottom without expanding includes reports the OPPOSITE of what is in force on this host. This is the single most likely way the REMOTE_ACCESS category produces a confidently wrong answer.

claim: `ss -ltnp` degrades by SILENT OMISSION as uid 1000: exit 0, header present, Process column blank, because inode-to-pid mapping needs /proc/<pid>/fd which is gated by a PTRACE_MODE_READ_FSCREDS check. /proc/net/tcp by contrast is fully readable and exposes the owning uid and socket inode for other users' sockets.
design_impact: 'A socket listens on :22 owned by uid 0' is provable; 'sshd owns it' is permanently unknown for another user's process. The listener check must claim exactly the first and explicitly decline the second — and must never use ss's blank column as evidence of anything.

claim: Ubuntu moved sshd to systemd socket activation at 1:9.0p1-1ubuntu1 (22.10); on 24.04 the listening port/address is derived from sshd_config by a systemd generator, and with Accept=no the listening fd moves from pid 1 to the service after first activation.
design_impact: Breaks both 'is sshd running' and 'who owns :22'. The sensor must assert the ACTIVATION PATH from world-readable unit files plus `systemctl is-active` (verified to work unprivileged), never a pid. Debian's actual ssh.socket text could not be fetched — see R1-OR10.

claim: Wazuh SCA's sshd rules are all `c:sshd -T` (cis_ubuntu24-04.yml:3523-3665) with no per-check unknown state, so run unprivileged they emit FALSE FAILS.
design_impact: A third piece of mature prior art committing the exact failure the brief calls critical — claiming to have checked when it could not. Together with osquery's silent-omission (R1-F32) and ipmitool's errno clobber (R1-F27), this is the strongest available argument that the UNKNOWN semantics are the real engineering content of this exercise.

claim: Lynis carries a SKIPREASON taxonomy at include/functions:2707-2764 — a ready-made enumeration of why a check did not run.
design_impact: Steal the TAXONOMY as the vocabulary for our `reason` field (EACCES / UTILITY_MISSING / UNSUPPORTED / TIMEOUT / BUDGET / ENOENT); reject Lynis's behaviour of skipping silently. GPLv3 means we take the idea and the vocabulary shape, never the code.

claim: XCCDF defines nine rule result values (pass, fail, error, unknown, notapplicable, notchecked, notselected, informational, fixed).
design_impact: Our fixed pass|fail|unknown vocabulary collapses error/unknown/notchecked/notapplicable into one value, so the `reason` field is where that distinction must live. Status is LIKELY, not VERIFIED: BOTH NIST primary URLs were BLOCKED (403/404) and the S6 attempt returned a landing page only. A blocked fetch is not a disproof.
